newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shed gains as Nikkei recovers.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shed gains as Nikkei recovers.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures slipped back from their highs on Monday as Nikkei cash and futures markets staged a partial recovery before the close.

"When the Nikkei collapsed, everyone was expecting a rally in Euroyen and JGBs but it didn't materialise. So those who were holding longs just dumped them back into the market," a trader at a Japanese brokerage said.
The 225-share Nikkei average fell below the key 19,500 level briefly before recovering to end 136.31 points lower at 19,668.07. Its September futures ended at 19,755 on SIMEX.
A report quoting Japan's Economic Planning Agency minister Taro Aso saying a rise in Japan's official discount rate was very possible by the end of this year also weighed on the market, dealers said.
The lead March Euroyen contract stood at 99.17 at 1105 GMT after trading a 99.16-99.21 range against an IMM close at 99.17.
September JGBs ended at 126.53 against a previous 126.72.
A dealer at a U.S. futures house said the Japanese interest rate market also came under some pressure from the yen's weakness and losses on U.S. treasury markets since Friday.
"But people still want to stay long on any dips," he said, adding that March Euroyen would be supported at 99.10/12.

The Japanese brokerage trader said March Euroyen could fall as low as 99.08 on stop-loss sales if it breached support at 99.15. "There'll just be a lot of long liquidations below 99.15 from those who've been buying Euroyen for the past two weeks."
The release of unexpectedly bullish U.S. economic data last Friday reignited expectations of a U.S. interest rate hike, bringing the prospect of a Japanese credit tightening back on the horizon.
Non-farm payrolls rose 316,000 in July, against market forecasts of a 193,000 increase while the unemployment rate slipped to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent in June.
Sharp rises in the National Association of Purchasing Management's indices of industry activity also added to fears of U.S. inflationary pressure, dealers said.
"The market is undergoing a correction after going up so much. If December Eurodollars break 94.10, we could go to 94.01/02," a dealer said.
December Eurodollars ended unchanged against an IMM close at 94.110. March was also steady at 94.025.
